issues.description: The problem statement describes the Developer property monthsOfSwiftExperience as type String, while both the template and the solution use an optional Int (Int?). The rest of the problem text (optional binding, checking equality to 1, incrementing by 1, example output like "12 months") clearly expects a numeric optional. Stating String in the problem statement contradicts the intended numeric design and can confuse students about the correct type to use or lead them to implement the wrong type if they follow the prose rather than the template.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the problem statement to specify monthsOfSwiftExperience as an optional Int (Int?) rather than String. For example: "The class should have two properties: name of type String and monthsOfSwiftExperience of type Int? (optional)." Also update the initializer example text to show passing an Int? (e.g. 36 or nil) so the prose, template, and solution consistently reflect that monthsOfSwiftExperience is numeric and optional.
